instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Every Loss Builds the Comeback
cards.instruction: Treat each setback as proof that the eventual victory will be more impressive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six losses! Keep every score sheet; I'll decide which one opens our comeback documentary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The tournament is over. Shall I pack the shirts away?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may label the box 'before the comeback.' Next season's opening shot will need those shirts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't a next season for us. The team is disbanding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take everyone's address before you close the box. I'll call them for the reunion. A team that has to find each other again before it wins gives us a much better ending.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave my collapsed cake where it is. I'll want a photograph of it beside the winning one; the contrast will be magnificent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've burned the oven out. Should I cancel the entry?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Find me a replacement oven. Winning after changing the whole kitchen will be a better story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The competition is tomorrow. The shop can only deliver at midnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Book midnight. I'll mix while we wait, and you photograph the delivery time. When that cake arrives at judging, they'll know how little night we had left to make it happen.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Congratulate Through Your Teeth
cards.instruction: Perform warm praise while allowing competitive resentment to intensify beneath every compliment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations on the prize! Come beside me; I'll present it. What a lovely year for judges willing to be surprised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you saying I didn't deserve it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not at all. You may be proud of how far they've stretched their idea of excellence for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just say 'well done' when you hand it over?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Well done. Hold it a little higher; I'll make sure everyone sees how warmly I welcome the entry that finished just ahead of mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful promotion. Come to the head of the table; I'll lead the toast. Such beautiful timing with the director's retirement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I worked for this. It wasn't just timing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Your patience has been splendidly rewarded by someone finally leaving you a chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you just be happy for me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delighted. Take the chair while I raise my glass. I look forward to seeing what you do with the opportunity the rest of us were still waiting to be offered.

cards.title: Nothing Without Stakes
cards.instruction: Price every request and decision with a reward, penalty, bargain, or trade.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can take my ladder once you've put aside the first sausage for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you lend it as a favour?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Put the favour down as lunch owed; I'll collect when the barbecue starts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can give you lunch, but I need you to hold the ladder too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make it two sausages. You climb, I'll hold, and bring my plate over before you start serving everyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll end this argument with my apology first, provided yours follows immediately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd like an apology without conditions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may have that if you take the first turn. I'll decide what mine owes you after I've heard it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'm sorry I called you selfish. Now can you apologise for leaving me all the washing-up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can offer the apology or tonight's washing-up. Choose one; I'm not paying twice for the same evening.

cards.title: Fair Means I Can Win
cards.instruction: Agree to any rule or bargain only after interpreting fairness in a way that preserves your advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. A fair race gives me a head start. I've had a tiring morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So has everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then compensate us proportionally. Mine involved stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We start on the same line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Move my portion of the line forward.

cards.title: Consequences Compound
cards.instruction: Make each new choice carry a larger reward, cost, audience, or point of no return.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Our table-tennis rematch decides who cleans up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. One game.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And whose cleaning method we use all year.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's not what I agreed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's ask the whole club to witness the clarification.
